diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the mesh $\bar \Omega ^{N}$, $ h_i \geq \bar h_i \geq h_{i+1}$ and $\sigma '(x) >0$
From Corollary \ref{Cor1}, we have that at all internal mesh points

issues.failure_explanation: The first line of the proof correctly gives L^N Z >= (alpha/(1-e^{-rho_i}))D^-Z - (alpha e^{-rho_{i+1}}/(1-e^{-rho_{i+1}}))D^+Z (with bar-rho). The final step replaces 1/(1-e^{-bar rho_i}) by 1/(1-e^{-bar rho_{i+1}}); since h_i >= h_{i+1} gives bar rho_i >= bar rho_{i+1}, one has 1/(1-e^{-bar rho_i}) <= 1/(1-e^{-bar rho_{i+1}}), so the inequality is reversed whenever h_i > h_{i+1} (the transition point). Counterexample: Z_i = min(x_i, 1-tau_x) has D^-Z >= 0, and at x_i = 1-tau_x, L^N Z = (h_i/bar h_i) bar a_i/(1-e^{-rho_i}) <= 2||a||/(1-e^{-rho_i}) while the claimed bound is alpha/(1-e^{-bar rho_{i+1}}) ~ alpha N/(4 ln N) for small eps. Lemma 4 then quotes an expression (missing the 1/h factors) derived from the false corollary to assert L^N e^{-alpha(1-x_i)/eps} >= 0, and Lemma 5 uses the corollary for the barrier e^{2x_i/alpha} at all internal points including the transition point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Corollary 1 to the correct two-denominator form (or to h_i = h_{i+1}) and verify L^N e^{-alpha(1-x_i)/eps} >= 0 and L^N e^{2x_i/alpha} >= e^{2x_i/alpha} directly from (finite-difference) at the transition point, using monotonicity of (1-e^{-t})/t and (e^t-1)/t; these direct computations succeed, so the barrier conclusions survive.
issues.overall_effect: The stated corollary is false at the mesh transition point, and the positivity of the barrier functions e^{-alpha(1-x_i)/eps} (Lemma 4, also used in Lemma 6) and e^{2x_i/alpha} (Lemmas 5, 6) is not established as written at that point; the layer-component bounds and hence Theorem 1 lose their proof at this step.
issues.title: Corollary 1 lower bound is false at the transition point; barrier positivity in Lemmas 4–5 rests on it
issues.why_classification: The conclusions are recoverable, but a contained replacement argument (direct sign analysis of the fitted operator at the non-uniform transition point) is required; the stated corollary itself must be corrected.

issues.failure_explanation: The truncation error bounds (trunc-error-sharp) and the final remark on delta_y^2 u - u_yy require |u_{xyy}| and, in the uniform fine y-region, ||u_{yyyy}||. Lemmas 4, 5 and 6 apply these to w_E, w_N (w_S) and w_{EN}, but (derivs-split-simple) and (derivs-split-ext) give only pure x- and pure y-derivative bounds for the layer functions, and for w_N, w_S no bound on the fourth y-derivative (nor on the first x-derivative appearing in sum_{n=1}^3) is stated anywhere. The claimed truncation estimates therefore rest on unestablished inputs.

\Vert  U - u\Vert  \leq C(N^{-1}\ln N)^2 +   CM^{-1}( M^{-1}\ln M)^{\frac{2}{3}}

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own appendix, the truncation error on a uniform x-mesh contains C h_i min{1,h_i/eps} eps|∂^3 u/∂x∂y^2| (the term (h/2) eps (Δu)_x from T_4). For u = w_N, differentiating L w_N = 0 gives eps w_{N,xyy} = (a w_{N,x})_x - eps w_{N,xxx}, which is O(1) throughout the characteristic layer y > 1-tau_y (indeed eps w_{0,yy} = a w_{0,x} for the leading parabolic-layer term) and carries no factor e^{-alpha(1-x)/eps}. On the coarse x-mesh (h_i = H ~ N^{-1}) with eps <~ H, this term is O(H) = O(N^{-1}), consistent with the fact that for rho >> 1 the scheme reduces to bar a_i D^-_x U - eps delta_y^2 U (upwind in x with y-diffusion lumped at x_i), which is only first order in x for parabolic layers. The lemma instead asserts the truncation error there is CM^{-2}(ln M)^2 + C (h_i^2/eps) e^{-alpha(1-x)/eps}, an exponential localisation near x = 1 that has no basis for w_N, and the barrier C(M^{-1}ln M)^2 x_i cannot absorb an O(N^{-1}) residual (L^N B_1 >= alpha/2 only). The claimed bound C(N^{-1}ln N)^2 + C(M^{-1}ln M)^2 for W_N - w_N (and W_S - w_S) is therefore unsupported and, generically (e.g. when f(x,1) ≠ 0 so w_0 ≠ 0), false uniformly in eps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either bound the O(h min{1,h/eps}) eps|w_{N,xyy}| term (which the source's own bounds show is O(h) on the coarse mesh) or modify the scheme (e.g. un-lump the y-diffusion to a Crank–Nicolson-type average in x) and redo the analysis; as written, Lemma 5 and Theorem 1 must be weakened to a first-order-in-N bound for the characteristic layer components.
issues.overall_effect: The nodal error bound for the characteristic layer components and hence the global parameter-uniform second-order (up to logs) bound of Theorem 1 are not established; the supported uniform bound for the x-direction in the presence of characteristic layers is only O(min{N^{-1}, N^{-2}/eps}), i.e. first order, which also undermines the abstract's claim of higher order than upwinding for problem (1).
issues.title: Lemma 5 misstates the truncation error for the characteristic layer on the coarse x-mesh: an O(h_i) term is dropped, so second order in x is not established
issues.why_classification: The central rate claim of the paper (parameter-uniform second order up to logarithms) cannot be recovered for the stated method with the stated analysis; any supported resolution materially worsens the advertised rate or changes the method.
